To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed a new e-genetics algorithm that can be used to identify genes from genome databases based on the structure of their encoded proteins, rather than the sequence; (2) we have used this algorithm to identify two new families of Drosophila genes that encode odor and taste receptors, respectively; and (3) these two new gene families are highly divergent and are not related to any previously identified G-protein-couple receptors.

a novel 'e- genetics' method of gene discovery, which is based on protein structure rather than sequence, has been developed and applied successfully to identify two new gene families of olfactory and gustatory receptors.

the identification of the genes that code for the receptors of the olfactory system and the taste system of Drosophila melanogaster, and with the elucidation of their molecular and cellular functions.
